source.title: Latent Communication in Artificial Neural Networks

record.tranche_reason: The thesis measures representation alignment and tests whether representations can be reused across independently trained models, using anchor-based relative representations, latent translations, similarity measures, and zero-shot stitching rather than the original sources' methods.
record.gate_note: The thesis contains extensive results on relative representations, latent-space translation, and stitching. Results cited from other works are not included. Rows below prioritize direct alignment or stitching results and selected outcomes showing dependence on projection choice. In the cross-modal section, the plotted stitching comparisons are not numerically recoverable from the text, so only the authors' explicit qualitative result is recorded.
record.test_reason: The thesis maps independently trained models' latent spaces onto each other and measures how well they align. It uses relative (anchor-based) representations, affine and orthogonal translation, and zero-shot stitching across seeds, architectures and modalities, and reports alignment and stitching scores. These bear directly on V3, V4 and V2 and, through the per-projection comparisons, on V6. It is not one of the original sources.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right. The authors conclude that independently trained networks' latent spaces are related by simple transforms, often angle-preserving or at most affine. These can be unified via relative representations or translated directly, enabling zero-shot stitching across seeds, architectures, languages and modalities when the semantic content is shared. They also report that the transformation class varies with dataset, architecture, modality and task (broader than orthogonal for autoencoders), and that only the data manifold, not the whole space, is alignable.
record.recipe_differences: The thesis develops anchor-based relative representations and direct latent translations, then tests alignment through retrieval, similarity, and zero-shot stitching. It does not use a scale-versus-capability sweep or test the Platonic Representation Hypothesis's scale trend.
record.method_sensitivity: Similarity metric and projection choice affect outcomes; the thesis also varies datasets, model architectures, modality, anchor count, and normalization. It reports no single projection as best across settings.
record.peer_reviewed: doctoral thesis; peer-review status not stated
record.problems: No model-scale or capability comparison is performed. Many claims are assessed through downstream stitching performance rather than a direct metric of pairwise-distance convergence. Cross-modal figure-level values are not recoverable from the supplied text. The thesis describes multiple methods and experiments, but the selected rows do not establish causal explanations for alignment.
record.rows_left_out: To stay within the 60-row limit while retaining results for each tested version, the record omits most rows from the full projection matrix in Table 7.3, other datasets and projections in Tables 4.1 and 5.3, and additional cross-architecture, cross-language, and stitching results in Tables 4.4–4.6, 5.1–5.2, 7.2, and 8.1–8.3. It also omits the ASIF and latent-space aggregation case studies because those sections summarize separate authored works and do not add a direct scale-convergence test.

untested.parts: No sweep of model scale. No convergence across different data, objectives or modalities as capability grows. The only capability–alignment evidence is Cora GNNs against one reference model (Fig. 4.3).
Whether cross-modal alignment increases as the vision and language models improve. Only existence and usefulness of the alignment is shown.
Unit-level or feature-level correspondence across seeds, and characterisation of the shared subspaces.
All of it: no interpretable neurons, SAE features or circuits are examined.
Neighbour-count settings and out-of-distribution inputs. OOD limits are only asserted in Ch. 1, not measured.
Whether alignment plateaus, and whether shared data or objectives cause it.

missing.what: Similarity-to-reference vs accuracy correlation across ~2000 GNNs (Pearson 0.955, models below 0.5 accuracy filtered out)

Cross-architecture stitching of pretrained encoders via translation. Affine/ortho come close to no-stitch: e.g. CIFAR-10 0.92–0.93 vs 0.95, TREC 0.82 vs 0.87, absolute 0.16/0.20. Linear with L2 normalisation drops to 0.44 on TREC.
Relative-representation stitching across languages and architectures, with large drops: text Rel stitch 75.89 vs 88.08; ImageNet1k ViT-B/16 decoder with RexNet encoder 30.78 vs 78.86
AE/VAE relative stitching across 5 seeds (AE MSE 2.83 vs 97.79 absolute on MNIST)
Cora per-projection stitching (cosine 0.53, Euclidean 0.27, L1 0.26, L∞ 0.12) and text ALBERT per-projection results
CKA similarity between pretrained models varies with the invariance projection and architecture; no single projection is best
Metric dependence within one alignment: ViT-B/16 vs ViT-S/16 relative spaces give cosine 0.97 but Jaccard 0.11 and MRR 0.27; FastText/Word2Vec give Jaccard 0.34 vs cosine 0.86
Transformation class differs by setting: pretrained classifier encoders are related mostly by orthogonal maps, while AE spaces need more than orthogonal (l-ortho lcos 0.78–0.85 vs affine 0.94–0.96)

record.verdict_notes: Doctoral thesis compiling the author's group's ICLR/NeurIPS papers. Rows r12–r20 likely have the RViT-B/16 and ViT-B/16 labels swapped; check against the PDF table. Combined-projection rows (r14, r17, r20, r22) are the authors' own method and should be read as best-case results. Many V4-relevant cross-architecture results (Tables 4.5–4.6, 5.1–5.2) are absent from the rows but central to V4.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep over model scale or capability, and no test of alignment increasing with scale or performance.
Cross-modal text/image stitching is tested on N24News with paired data; no scale or performance sweep of the two modalities is reported.
Tests include same-architecture autoencoders trained with different seeds and GNN stitching across seeds. It does not test whether the same individual units recur or characterize shared features.

Tests anchor-based relative representations and affine or orthogonal translations, including stitching. It does not test every mapping type listed in the claim, such as unpaired mapping or layer stitching.
No recurrence of interpretable neurons, SAE features, or circuits is tested.
Tests changes across similarity metrics and projection choices, but not neighbour-count settings or out-of-distribution effects as a systematic convergence analysis.
The thesis discusses partial manifold alignment and varying training factors, but does not test whether shared data or objectives cause alignment, nor whether alignment plateaus.
